title: Machine learning-derived identification of tumor-infiltrating immune cell-related signature for improving prognosis and immunotherapy responses in patients with skin cutaneous melanoma.
summary: A machine-learning-derived immune signature stratifies melanoma prognosis and anti-PD-1 response associations across public and in-house cohorts. The reported result is retrospective prognostic association, not causal immune mechanism or prospective treatment benefit.
ai_technology: Machine-learning analysis applies the stated model to the paper’s medicine dataset and evaluates the reported outcome.
organization: Department of Dermatovenereology, The Seventh Affiliated Hospital of Sun Yat-Sen University, Shenzhen, China

evidence.tested: A machine-learning-derived immune signature stratifies melanoma prognosis and anti-PD-1 response associations across public and in-house cohorts. The reported result is retrospective prognostic association, not causal immune mechanism or prospective treatment benefit.
evidence.unknown: Results are limited to the reported models, cohorts, datasets or experiments; broader generalization and clinical or operational benefit were not established.
